title: Modernizing Ground Truth: Four Shifts Toward Improving Reliability and Validity in AI in Education

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the risk of human annotators uncritically adopting incorrect AI-generated pre-labels by monitoring changes in human accuracy during human-AI collaborative annotation.
Using targeted audits and complementary validity checks to evaluate if Large Language Model (LLM) judges systematically overvalue responses containing citations.
Using targeted audits and complementary validity checks to evaluate if Large Language Model (LLM) judges systematically favor technical formatting over pedagogical correctness.
Auditing LLM outputs to identify if the model systematically favors specific options based on their order in pairwise comparisons.

Employing inter-rater reliability (IRR) as a diagnostic tool, using multilabel annotations, expert-based reconciliation, and predictive validity checks to detect shared systematic misconceptions and directional errors among human raters.
Evaluating synthetic ground truth data generated by LLMs to check if recursive training amplifies surface-level stylistic patterns at the expense of pedagogical precision.
